<img src="../man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="140" />

VirtualDairyHerdR simulates two types of precision livestock farming sensor
data — daily activity collar/tag data via `simulate_activity()`, and
high-frequency internal bolus sensor data via `simulate_bolus()`.

Both are modelled on the output of real commercial sensor platforms used on
Irish grass-based dairy farms, including bolus and collar-based systems that
continuously monitor temperature, rumination, and activity.

---

## Sensor types

| Function | Type | Resolution | Modelled on |
|---|---|---|---|
| `simulate_activity()` | Collar / tag | Daily snapshot | Collar-based activity tags |
| `simulate_bolus()` | Internal bolus | User-defined (default 10 mins) | Bolus sensor platforms |

---

## Daily activity data — `simulate_activity()`

`simulate_activity()` generates a daily snapshot of activity for each cow.
It accepts the output of `simulate_herd()` and adds four columns.

```{r activity-generate}
herd     <- simulate_herd(100, seed = 42)
activity <- simulate_activity(herd, seed = 42)
head(activity[, c("cow_id", "breed", "days_in_milk", "activity_score",
                  "steps", "lying_minutes", "standing_minutes")])
```

Lying and standing minutes always sum to 1440 — a hard biological constraint.

```{r activity-check}
all(activity$lying_minutes + activity$standing_minutes == 1440)
```

### Activity score declines with DIM

Activity is highest in early lactation and declines gradually as cows settle
into mid and late lactation.

```{r activity-dim}
activity |>
  ggplot(aes(x = days_in_milk, y = activity_score, colour = breed)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 1.2) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    title  = "Activity score over DIM by breed",
    x      = "Days in Milk",
    y      = "Activity score",
    colour = "Breed"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Lying time vs activity

Higher activity cows spend less time lying — the inverse relationship mirrors
real sensor data.

```{r lying-activity}
activity |>
  ggplot(aes(x = activity_score, y = lying_minutes, colour = breed)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 1.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    title  = "Lying time vs activity score",
    x      = "Activity score",
    y      = "Lying minutes per day",
    colour = "Breed"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Steps distribution by breed

```{r steps-breed}
activity |>
  ggplot(aes(x = breed, y = steps, fill = breed)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.alpha = 0.3) +
  labs(
    title = "Daily steps by breed",
    x     = NULL,
    y     = "Steps per day"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

---

## High-frequency bolus data — `simulate_bolus()`

`simulate_bolus()` generates continuous sensor readings at a user-defined
interval (default 10 minutes), producing the kind of data stream you would
see exported from a bolus sensor platform.

### Key arguments

| Argument | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `herd` | — | Output of `simulate_herd()` |
| `days` | 30 | Days of sensor data per cow |
| `interval_mins` | 10 | Recording interval in minutes |
| `start_date` | `Sys.Date()` | Start date for records |
| `seed` | NULL | Reproducibility |

```{r bolus-generate}
bolus_herd <- simulate_herd(5, seed = 42)
bolus      <- simulate_bolus(bolus_herd, days = 21, interval_mins = 10,
                              seed = 42)

# Dimensions: 5 cows x 21 days x 144 readings/day
nrow(bolus)
head(bolus)
```

---

## Biological patterns

### Temperature — circadian rhythm

Internal body temperature follows a circadian rhythm with a daily minimum
around 05:00 and maximum around 15:00 (amplitude ~0.5°C). This mirrors the
pattern recorded by real bolus sensors on farm.

```{r temp-circadian}
# Single cow, first 3 days
cow1 <- bolus |> dplyr::filter(cow_id == unique(bolus$cow_id)[1])

cow1 |>
  dplyr::filter(date %in% unique(cow1$date)[1:3]) |>
  dplyr::mutate(hour = as.numeric(format(timestamp, "%H")) +
                       as.numeric(format(timestamp, "%M")) / 60) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = hour, y = bolus_temp,
             colour = factor(date), group = factor(date))) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title  = "Circadian temperature pattern — 3 days at 10-minute intervals",
    x      = "Hour of day",
    y      = "Internal temperature (°C)",
    colour = "Date"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Temperature — mastitis and oestrus spikes

Mastitis raises temperature by +0.5 to +2.5°C. Oestrus raises it by +0.3
to +0.8°C. Both are detectable against the circadian baseline.

```{r temp-events}
cow1_daily <- cow1 |>
  dplyr::group_by(date, oestrus, mastitis) |>
  dplyr::summarise(mean_temp = mean(bolus_temp), .groups = "drop")

cow1 |>
  ggplot(aes(x = timestamp, y = bolus_temp)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.35, colour = "#607D8B") +
  geom_rect(
    data = dplyr::filter(cow1_daily, oestrus),
    aes(xmin = as.POSIXct(date), xmax = as.POSIXct(date) + 86400,
        ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
    fill = "#FF9800", alpha = 0.2, inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_rect(
    data = dplyr::filter(cow1_daily, mastitis),
    aes(xmin = as.POSIXct(date), xmax = as.POSIXct(date) + 86400,
        ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
    fill = "#F44336", alpha = 0.2, inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Internal temperature over 21 days",
    subtitle = "Orange = oestrus  |  Red = mastitis",
    x        = "Date",
    y        = "Temperature (°C)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Rumination — post-feeding peaks

Rumination peaks twice daily (~08:00 and ~20:00) following feeding. It is
suppressed during oestrus (near zero) and reduced 30–60% during mastitis.

```{r rumination-pattern}
cow1 |>
  dplyr::filter(date %in% unique(cow1$date)[1:5]) |>
  dplyr::mutate(hour = as.numeric(format(timestamp, "%H")) +
                       as.numeric(format(timestamp, "%M")) / 60,
                event = dplyr::case_when(
                  oestrus  ~ "Oestrus",
                  mastitis ~ "Mastitis",
                  TRUE     ~ "Normal"
                )) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = hour, y = rumination_mins,
             colour = event, group = factor(date))) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(
    "Normal"   = "#2196F3",
    "Oestrus"  = "#FF9800",
    "Mastitis" = "#F44336"
  )) +
  labs(
    title  = "Rumination pattern — post-feeding peaks and event suppression",
    x      = "Hour of day",
    y      = "Rumination (mins per 10-min interval)",
    colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Activity — oestrus spike detection

The oestrus activity spike is the primary detection signal on commercial bolus
platforms. It is 2–3× baseline and lasts 12–18 hours.

```{r activity-oestrus}
cow1 |>
  dplyr::group_by(date, oestrus, mastitis) |>
  dplyr::summarise(mean_activity = mean(activity_index), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = date, y = mean_activity, fill = oestrus)) +
  geom_col(alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("FALSE" = "#2196F3", "TRUE" = "#FF9800"),
    labels = c("Normal", "Oestrus")
  ) +
  labs(
    title  = "Mean daily activity — oestrus spike detection",
    x      = "Date",
    y      = "Mean activity index",
    fill   = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Custom intervals

The `interval_mins` argument lets you match the resolution of any sensor
platform. Common values:

```{r custom-interval}
# 15-minute intervals
bolus_15 <- simulate_bolus(bolus_herd, days = 7, interval_mins = 15, seed = 42)
nrow(bolus_15)  # 5 cows x 7 days x 96 readings/day

# 30-minute intervals
bolus_30 <- simulate_bolus(bolus_herd, days = 7, interval_mins = 30, seed = 42)
nrow(bolus_30)  # 5 cows x 7 days x 48 readings/day
```

---

## Joining bolus data to milk records

Because `cow_id` is consistent across all pipeline functions, bolus data joins
cleanly to milk, health, and fertility records.

```{r join-bolus-milk}
milk <- simulate_milk(bolus_herd, seed = 42)

# Daily bolus summary per cow
bolus_daily <- bolus |>
  dplyr::group_by(cow_id, date) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean_temp       = round(mean(bolus_temp), 2),
    total_rumination = round(sum(rumination_mins), 1),
    mean_activity   = round(mean(activity_index), 2),
    oestrus         = any(oestrus),
    mastitis        = any(mastitis),
    .groups         = "drop"
  )

# Join to milk snapshot
dplyr::left_join(milk[, c("cow_id", "milk_kg", "scc")],
                 dplyr::filter(bolus_daily, date == min(bolus_daily$date)),
                 by = "cow_id") |>
  head(10)
```

---

## Use cases

- **Oestrus detection** — use the activity spike + temperature rise as features
  in a classification model
- **Mastitis early warning** — temperature + rumination suppression as a
  combined alert signal
- **Anomaly detection** — train unsupervised models on normal circadian patterns
  and flag deviations
- **Sensor fusion** — join bolus data with milk recording to model the
  relationship between rumination and milk yield
